headline: Logit perturbations reproduce many reported Neural Thickets gains without changing weights
summary: A preprint re-evaluates the Neural Thickets perturb-select-vote procedure and reports that much of its measured gain does not require perturbing model weights. The authors apply a fixed random bias to output logits, select members using 200 labeled task examples, then vote across selected members. In author-reported tests on language models up to 7B parameters, this approach is statistically indistinguishable from full-weight perturbations on 22 of 28 matched model–task pairs and significantly better on three and worse on three; effects vary by task, and on USPTO the raw accuracy partly reflects a majority-class predictor. On vision tasks with train-test shift, the authors attribute gains primarily to output recalibration. The work offers an alternative explanation for the measured gains, not evidence that nearby weight-space structure is absent or that the method improves general model capability.
